When Anushka Sharma arrived at UMass Dartmouth 
from a small village in Haryana, India, she came to earn a 
master's degree in chemistry. Two years later, she leaves 
behind something far greater, a stronger, more connected 
campus community. 
Long before studying abroad, Anushka served as 
President of her college's Rotary Club, affiliated with 
Rotary International, where she discovered a belief that 
still guides her today: the greatest measure of success 
isn't how far you go—it's how many people you help move 
forward with you. 
While pursuing graduate research in chemistry, Anushka 
became one of UMass Dartmouth's most engaged 
student leaders, stepping into more than a dozen formal 
and informal leadership, mentoring, research, and service 
roles. 
Whether welcoming international students, mentoring 
first-generation students, teaching, tutoring, organizing 
campus initiatives, or simply being someone students 
could count on, every role shared the same purpose: 
helping others feel supported, empowered, and that they 
belonged. 
Driven by the belief that every international student 
deserved a place to belong, Anushka co-founded the 
Association of International Students, creating one 
welcoming community where students from every culture 
could connect and celebrate their identities through 
initiatives such as Global Fusion. 
Her commitment to scholarship and service earned her 
the Academic Excellence Award presented by Stemming 
While Black, followed by the Donald C. Howard Pillar of 
the Community Award, one of UMass Dartmouth's highest 
honors for student leadership and community impact. 
Anushka Sharma '26 
Chemistry, MS 
"I've always believed 
that success means very 
little if it only changes 
your own life. Real 
success is using every 
opportunity you've been 
given to open doors for 
someone else. 
If, years from now, 
people remember that 
they felt supported, 
valued, and that they 
belonged, then I will 
know I lived the kind 
of leadership I always 
believed in." 
STUDENT SPOTLIGHT
